source.title: Learning Dynamics in Continual Pre-Training for Large Language Models
source.authors: Xingjin Wang; Howe Tissue; Lu Wang; Lin-Jing Li; D. Zeng

record.tranche_reason: The study measures validation-loss dynamics during continual pre-training and tests a CPT-specific scaling law, rather than reproducing the original parameter/token/compute sweeps.
record.gate_note: The study tests continual-pretraining loss dynamics, including power-law distribution-shift terms and predictions across schedules and settings. It does not test downstream-task performance, a compute-optimal parameter/token allocation, architecture-shape effects, or the original pretraining laws’ extrapolation from small runs to orders-of-magnitude larger runs. The out-of-domain linear-combination results are validation-loss estimates, not downstream-task performance.
record.test_reason: The study fits and predicts held-out validation loss of language models during continual pre-training (CPT), a transfer regime. The law has a power-law term in summed learning rate (a proxy for training amount), a power-law distribution-shift term and an N^-γ model-size term. It compares this power-law form against an exponential form. That is a new training regime with a result bearing on V5. It is T3 rather than T2 because it does not reproduce the original N/D/C sweeps aimed at the same question.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that a CPT scaling law combining power-law distribution shift with learning-rate annealing predicts Dpt and Dcpt validation loss at any CPT step and under various schedules. They say it extends to model size, replay ratio, batch size and sequence length, and to open-source models with unknown pretraining details. They also use it to choose loss potential, peak learning rate and replay ratio, and predict out-of-domain loss through a linear combination of Dpt and Dcpt losses.
record.recipe_differences: The study proposes a CPT-specific loss-dynamics equation combining an annealing law with a distribution-shift term; it does not reproduce the original pretraining parameter/token/compute sweeps.
record.method_sensitivity: The measured loss dynamics and fitted terms vary with learning-rate schedule, CPT data distribution, replay ratio, model size, and batch-size/sequence-length setting.

fits_no_version.finding: Out-of-domain validation loss during CPT is predicted as a linear combination of Dpt and Dcpt losses, with absolute errors below 0.003 (Figs. 9, 21, 22).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Loss on unseen domains during CPT is a fixed linear combination of the losses on the pretraining and CPT domains.

fits_no_version.finding: Replay ratio changes the distribution-shift and annealing terms in an exponential, not power-law, form (Eq. 8). Higher replay gives a smaller shift.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Data-mixture ratio effects on loss follow an exponential form (as in the data mixing law).

fits_no_version.finding: Higher loss potential (less annealed pretrained model) yields lower final Dcpt loss (Fig. 5).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Pretrained checkpoints with less learning-rate annealing adapt better in CPT.

record.problems: The authors describe the work as empirical and note a lack of rigorous theoretical analysis. The main model-size experiments cover only 106M to 1.7B non-embedding parameters, below mainstream LLM scales; many results are presented in figures without numerical uncertainty estimates.
record.rows_left_out: No additional reported results bearing on the tested version were left out.

untested.parts: No parameter, token or compute sweep of pretraining loss with the other factors non-bottlenecked.
No extrapolation from small runs to runs orders of magnitude larger. Prediction is only to later steps or other schedules.
Other modalities, repeated-data regimes and fine-tuning beyond CPT are not tested. Model sizes above 1.7B are not tested; the authors flag this.
Only validation losses are measured, not downstream task performance.
Disagreement among published N/D/C laws and their exponents is not tested.

missing.what: Distribution-shift term nearly coincides across 106M, 594M and 1720M models under constant learning rate.
Separate Eq. 4 fits for 594M and 1720M give degenerate shift parameters (e.g. B=29.121, β=0.001), indicating weakly identified power-law terms.
Eq. 4 fitted per replay ratio (Fig. 12), and unified Eq. 8 fits across replay ratios (Fig. 19).
Alternative annealing forms give similar fits (Dpt R² 0.9944–0.9952; Dcpt 0.9983–0.9993).

record.verdict_notes: Neither original source; no self-overlap. Scales are small (≤1.7B) and there are no uncertainty estimates. Some fitted exponents are extreme or degenerate (r15, r16, Fig. 16), so the power-law terms are flexible rather than tightly constrained. This is relevant to V7 but does not concern the N/D/C laws, so V7 is left untested.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not test held-out pretraining loss as a power law in parameters, tokens, or compute with the other quantities non-bottlenecked.
It predicts CPT loss at later training steps and under other learning-rate schedules, not loss of runs orders of magnitude larger predicted from smaller runs.
No fixed-compute sweep or compute-optimal parameter/token allocation is tested.
Depth, width, and other architecture details are not varied.
Tests continual pre-training of language models only; it does not test other modalities, repeated-data pretraining, or fine-tuning and transfer regimes other than CPT.
The study measures validation loss, not downstream-task performance.
The study does not test disagreement in the original parameter/token/compute laws, their compute-optimal splits, or whether those laws’ fitted exponents vary with counting and fitting choices.

rows.subject: LLaMA3.2-1B (Model I)
rows.operation_detail: Fit on fewer CPT steps and predict later validation losses using a proxy Dpt dataset.
rows.measure: Predicted versus observed CPT validation-loss curve
rows.note: The text says Equation 4 effectively predicts later losses for the proxy Dpt and true Dcpt.
rows.check: Fitted parameters are extreme (A=11.123, α=7.122 on proxy Dpt; β up to 35.3 on Pile of Law). The power-law exponents are poorly constrained here.

source_check.correct: State relative to V5: partial. Model I uses the augmented Equation 4. Its proxy-Dpt fit has A=11.123 and α=7.122; its Pile-of-Law shift exponent is β=12.195. β=35.333 belongs to Model II.
source_check.problem: The full-curve result qualifies V5; the verdict fix also attributes Model II's exponent to Model I and asserts poor constraint without reported parameter uncertainty.

relationships.condition: CPT of LLaMA-like models (106M–1.7B) and LLaMA3.2-1B on FineWeb to Knowledge Pile or Pile of Law, validation loss on Dpt and Dcpt
relationships.reason: The power-law shift form beats the exponential form (R² 0.994 vs 0.926; 0.985 vs 0.801). Eq. 4 and Eq. 7 fit and predict curves across schedules, sizes, batch settings, datasets and open-source models (r1,r2,r5-r10,r13-r16).
relationships.display_finding: The power-law shift component outperformed an exponential form with R² of 0.994 versus 0.926 and 0.985 versus 0.801, while full-curve predictions required distribution-shift and annealing terms.

relation.reason: It compares power-law and exponential distribution-shift forms and tests an extended loss law across CPT settings.

tranche.reason: The study supplies direct validation-loss results in continual pre-training, a transfer setting covered by V5.

source_check.notes: Figure 17's legend and caption disagree about the larger batch/sequence setting; the listed row conditions reproduce the legend. Figure 18 supplies fitted exponents but no uncertainty estimates establishing that they are poorly constrained.

statements.correction: Scheduled CPT: Equation 4 combines power-law terms in summed learning rate with separate PT and CPT learning-rate annealing terms; full loss curves depend on learning-rate history. The statement gives no numerical claim about this study.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: CPT validation-loss distribution shifts and predictions in the tested language-model settings
reader_labels.reason: The shift term is reported to follow a power-law form, and the CPT-specific law fits or predicts curves across tested schedules, model sizes, replay ratios, batch/sequence settings, and datasets (r1-r2, r5-r16).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: The full curves are modeled by combining learning-rate-annealing terms with a power-law distribution-shift term, not by showing that the entire validation-loss curve follows the same simple power law (r3-r4).
